intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04)
intervention_dose: doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 IV + trabectedin 1.1 mg/m2 IV q3w x6, then trabectedin maintenance; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6
indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma (uterine and soft-tissue), chemotherapy-naive
population_detail: ECOG 0-1; 67 of 150 patients had uterine LMS; randomisation stratified by uterine vs soft-tissue origin; surgery for residual disease allowed after 6 cycles
outcome: median PFS by blinded independent central review
safety_summary: Combination markedly more myelotoxic than doxorubicin alone: G3-4 neutropenia 80% vs 13%, thrombocytopenia 47% vs 0%, febrile neutropenia 28% vs 9%. One treatment-related death, in the doxorubicin-alone arm (cardiac failure).
notes: The regimen her oncologist has planned. Uterine LMS was 45% of the trial and a stratification factor, but the abstract does not report a uterine-only PFS estimate; the benefit claim for her rests on the stratified full-trial analysis. AE rates from the published abstract.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + trabectedin, then trabectedin maintenance (LMS-04, final OS)
intervention_dose: as in the primary report: doxorubicin 60 mg/m2 + trabectedin 1.1 mg/m2 q3w x6, then trabectedin maintenance
indication: metastatic or unresectable leiomyosarcoma (uterine and soft-tissue), chemotherapy-naive
population_detail: same 150-patient ITT population as the primary report; median follow-up 55 months; analyses adjusted for uterine vs soft-tissue origin and disease stage
design: randomised open-label phase 3 (LMS-04, NCT02997358), final overall-survival analysis
safety_summary: Abstract states AE incidence and dose reductions were higher with the combination; no new per-term rates given. Per-term safety is carried on the primary-report row (pmid 35835135).
notes: The OS confirmation that separates LMS-04 from every other first-line intensification attempt in this disease. Fallback for per-term AEs attempted: abstract has none, NEJM is not in PMC, publisher is paywalled; the trial's per-term safety table is on the companion Lancet Oncol row.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + ifosfamide (EORTC 62012)
intervention_dose: doxorubicin 25 mg/m2/day d1-3 + ifosfamide 10 g/m2 over 4 days with mesna and pegfilgrastim, q3w; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2
indication: advanced or metastatic high-grade soft-tissue sarcoma, first line
population_detail: age 18-60, WHO PS 0-1; all STS histologies, not LMS- or uterine-specific
outcome: median overall survival (primary endpoint, not met)
safety_summary: Intensified combination roughly doubles to quadruples high-grade haematologic toxicity versus doxorubicin alone; febrile neutropenia 46% vs 13% despite pegfilgrastim.
notes: Doubles the response rate without an OS win, at real toxicity cost; the authors themselves restrict it to situations where tumour shrinkage is the goal. Age cap 60 means she would have been eligible. All-comer STS, so LMS-specific benefit is not established here.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel (GeDDiS)
intervention_dose: gemcitabine 675 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 75 mg/m2 d8 q3w x6; comparator doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 q3w x6
indication: previously untreated advanced or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma
population_detail: Trojani grade 2-3 STS; leiomyosarcoma (uterine and non-uterine) was the largest histology stratum
outcome: proportion alive and progression-free at 24 weeks (primary endpoint: no difference)
safety_summary: No efficacy advantage for gem-doce, and toxicity profiles differ rather than favour it: more fatigue, less mucositis and febrile neutropenia than doxorubicin. No treatment-related deaths.
notes: The trial that kept doxorubicin as the default first line: gem-doce was not better and trended worse on PFS. Relevant to her as the strongest randomised argument against choosing gem-doce over an anthracycline backbone up front, GOG-0250's uterine-specific single-arm activity notwithstanding.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel, first-line uterine LMS (GOG phase 2)
intervention_dose: gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 over 90 min d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 with G-CSF, q21d; doses reduced after prior pelvic radiation
indication: metastatic uterine leiomyosarcoma, chemotherapy-naive
population_detail: 42 women with advanced uLMS, no prior chemotherapy; 39 evaluable for response
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 4.4 mo; median response duration 6 mo
safety_summary: Myelosuppression dominates: G3-4 neutropenia 17%, G3 anemia 24%, G3 fatigue 17%. One possibly related G4 pulmonary toxicity, which matters for a patient with infiltrative bilateral lung disease at altitude.
notes: The uterine-specific first-line benchmark for gem-doce: response in a third of patients but short mPFS. Read alongside GeDDiS before treating the 35.8% as superiority over doxorubicin; single-arm response rates in uLMS have repeatedly outrun randomised comparisons.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel in leiomyosarcoma (first phase 2, mixed line)
intervention_dose: gemcitabine 900 mg/m2 d1,8 + docetaxel 100 mg/m2 d8 with G-CSF d9-15, q21d; 25% dose reduction after pelvic radiation
indication: unresectable leiomyosarcoma, uterine-dominant (29 of 34 uterine)
population_detail: 0-2 prior regimens; 16 of 34 had progressed on doxorubicin, 18 chemotherapy-naive
safety_summary: Haematologic toxicity common but febrile neutropenia rare (6%); no bleeding events.
notes: The study that established gem-doce in LMS, and the source of the often-quoted 53% response rate. Activity held in doxorubicin-pretreated patients, which is why this regimen remains her most likely second-line chemotherapy after LMS-04.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + docetaxel +/- bevacizumab (GOG-0250)
intervention_dose: gemcitabine-docetaxel plus bevacizumab or placebo
indication: chemotherapy-naive metastatic unresectable uterine leiomyosarcoma
population_detail: 107 of a planned 130 patients; accrual stopped early for futility
outcome: median PFS (bevacizumab did not improve it)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 6.2 mo (placebo) vs 4.2 mo (bevacizumab); mean DoR 8.6 vs 8.8 mo
safety_summary: No significant G3-4 differences between arms; bevacizumab added hypertension (8% G3) and a fistula without any efficacy return.
notes: The uterine-LMS-specific test of adding plain VEGF blockade to first-line chemotherapy, and it failed. Directly relevant when weighing the PD-1xVEGF bispecific rationale for the ivonescimab trial seat: anti-VEGF alone bought nothing in this exact disease. Per-term AE rates from the PMC full text (Table 2, n=103 toxicity-evaluable).

intervention_label: Trabectedin (ET743-SAR-3007 phase 3)
intervention_dose: trabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 24-h IV infusion d1 q21d; comparator dacarbazine 1 g/m2 q3w
indication: metastatic liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline and at least one further regimen
population_detail: 518 patients; L-sarcomas only; leiomyosarcoma 73% of enrolment
safety_summary: Myelosuppression and transient transaminitis define the profile; treatment-related deaths 2.1%, all in the trabectedin arm.
notes: Basis of trabectedin's US approval in L-sarcomas: disease control without an OS difference. Per-term G3-4 rates from the PMC full text. If she receives trabectedin inside LMS-04, this later-line monotherapy row becomes less relevant to her own sequence.

intervention_label: Trabectedin vs dacarbazine, uterine LMS subgroup
intervention_dose: trabectedin 1.5 mg/m2 24-h IV q3w; dacarbazine 1 g/m2 q3w
indication: advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after anthracycline failure
population_detail: 232 uLMS patients (trabectedin 144, dacarbazine 88), the largest subgroup (40%) of the phase 3 trial; post hoc analysis
design: post hoc subgroup analysis of a randomised phase 3 (NCT01343277)
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 4.0 mo (trabectedin) vs 1.5 mo (dacarbazine); mDoR 6.5 vs 4.1 mo
safety_summary: In the uLMS subset the trabectedin profile matches the full trial: G3/4 transaminitis 34% (ALT), neutropenia 36%, with cytopenias and two treatment-related deaths in the overall trabectedin arm.
notes: The uterine-specific read of SAR-3007: PFS benefit holds in her histology, response rates stay near 10%, and OS does not move. Post hoc, so treat the subgroup HR as estimation rather than confirmation. Per-term AE rates from the PMC full text.

intervention_label: Pazopanib (PALETTE)
intervention_dose: pazopanib 800 mg PO daily
indication: metastatic non-adipocytic soft-tissue sarcoma after standard chemotherapy
population_detail: 369 patients, angiogenesis-inhibitor-naive; leiomyosarcoma was the largest histology group
safety_summary: Class-typical VEGFR-TKI profile: fatigue, diarrhoea, nausea, weight loss, hypertension. Abstract reports any-grade rates; G3 detail is in the full paper.
notes: Approval trial for pazopanib in pretreated STS. PFS gain of 3 months, no OS gain. The uterine-sarcoma-specific read is on the Benson retrospective row.

intervention_label: Pazopanib in uterine sarcoma (EORTC 62043/62072 retrospective)
intervention_dose: pazopanib 800 mg PO daily
indication: advanced uterine sarcoma (39 of 44 uterine LMS), heavily pretreated
population_detail: 44 uterine sarcoma patients pooled from EORTC phase 2 (62043) and PALETTE (62072); 61% had >=2 prior chemotherapy lines; 84% high grade
design: retrospective analysis of two prospective trials

outcomes.name: OS
outcomes.notes: vs 11.1 months non-uterine; difference not significant

safety_summary: No uterine-specific safety analysis; toxicity in the parent trials matches the PALETTE profile on the companion row.
notes: Confirms pazopanib activity reaches uterine LMS at roughly the same modest level as other STS. AE fallback: abstract has no per-term data, no PMC record, publisher paywalled; safety is carried on the PALETTE row for the same drug and dose.

intervention_label: Eribulin (phase 3 vs dacarbazine)
intervention_dose: eribulin mesilate 1.4 mg/m2 IV d1,8 q21d; comparator dacarbazine 850-1200 mg/m2 d1 q21d
indication: advanced liposarcoma or leiomyosarcoma, >=2 prior regimens including an anthracycline
population_detail: 452 patients; LMS and liposarcoma randomised as independent strata
safety_summary: G3+ AEs 67% vs 56% with dacarbazine; on-treatment deaths 4% vs 1%, one considered treatment-related. Neutropenia is the characteristic high-grade event.
notes: The trial-level OS benefit was driven by the liposarcoma stratum (see the excluded Demetri 2017 subgroup row); the LMS subgroup did not share the OS advantage, so eribulin sits low among her later-line options despite the positive headline. Abstract reports only pooled G3+ rates; per-term table is in the full paper.

intervention_label: Gemcitabine + dacarbazine (Spanish GEIS randomised phase 2)
intervention_dose: gemcitabine 1800 mg/m2 at 10 mg/m2/min + dacarbazine 500 mg/m2 q2w; comparator dacarbazine 1200 mg/m2 q3w
indication: previously treated advanced soft-tissue sarcoma
population_detail: 113 patients, mixed STS histologies including LMS; not uterine-specific

outcomes.name: DCR
outcomes.notes: objective response or stable disease; 25% dacarbazine

safety_summary: Well tolerated; granulocytopenia the main serious event, febrile neutropenia uncommon, discontinuation for toxicity rare. Abstract gives no per-term percentages.
notes: A gemcitabine-based fallback with an OS signal in a small randomised phase 2; mixed histologies, so LMS-specific benefit is inferred rather than shown. AE fallback: abstract qualitative only, no PMC record, publisher paywalled.

intervention_label: Temozolomide in soft-tissue sarcoma (LMS-enriched activity)
intervention_dose: temozolomide 200 mg/m2 oral bolus then 90 mg/m2 q12h x9 doses, q4w
indication: unresectable or metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma, previously treated
population_detail: 25 evaluable patients; all responders had uterine or non-uterine LMS; LMS subset n=11
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 2.0 mo overall; 3.9 mo in the LMS subset
safety_summary: Gentle by chemotherapy standards: no G4 events or treatment-related deaths; single G3 events (nausea, anemia, fatigue, alkaline phosphatase, non-neutropenic fever).
notes: Modest single-agent activity concentrated in LMS; today temozolomide's real interest for her is as the partner in olaparib-temozolomide rather than as monotherapy.

intervention_label: Olaparib + temozolomide (NCI Protocol 10250)
intervention_dose: olaparib 200 mg PO BID d1-7 + temozolomide 75 mg/m2 PO daily d1-7, q21d
indication: advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma after progression on >=1 prior line
population_detail: 22 evaluable uLMS patients; 59% had >=3 prior lines; HRD not required for entry but assessed on paired biopsies (RAD51 assay, WES/RNAseq)
outcome: best ORR within 6 months (primary endpoint, met: >=5 of 22 required)

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: primary endpoint, 5 of 22 within 6 months; design 93% power, alpha 0.06

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: HR-deficient by RAD51 assay; 31% (5 of 16) had deleterious HR-gene alterations by WES

safety_summary: Haematologic toxicity is the cost: G3/4 neutropenia 75% and thrombocytopenia 32%, managed with dose modification; no treatment-related deaths reported.
notes: The strongest targeted-combination signal in her exact histology, but it sits one line away: entry required prior therapy. Entry did not require HRD, and half of assayed tumours were RAD51-deficient; her own HRD/BRCA status is unmeasured, which is exactly why tissue testing gates this branch. A randomised phase 2/3 confirmation (NCT05432791) has completed accrual. Published erratum (pmid 37801676) does not change the efficacy results.

intervention_label: PARP inhibition in BRCA2-altered uterine LMS (genomic series)
intervention_dose: PARP inhibitor, agent per treating physician (case series)
indication: leiomyosarcoma; BRCA2-altered uterine LMS subset
population_detail: 2,548 STS genomic profiles across two cohorts; BRCA2 alterations concentrated in uLMS (10% of uLMS); 4 uLMS patients with functional BRCA2 loss treated with PARP inhibitors
design: retrospective genomic analysis plus 4-patient case series
outcome: durable clinical benefit on PARP inhibition (descriptive)

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: BRCA2-lost uLMS on PARP inhibitors; response durations in full text

outcomes.name: biomarker
outcomes.notes: BRCA2 alteration prevalence in uLMS vs 1% in unselected STS

safety_summary: No systematic AE reporting; four-patient off-label series.
notes: Why BRCA2 testing earns its place on her tissue-NGS order: the one STS subtype where BRCA2 loss clusters is hers. Hypothesis-generating only; the prospective data live on the NCI 10250 row. AE data not reported in source beyond case narratives.

intervention_label: Tazemetostat in INI1/SMARCB1-lost epithelioid sarcoma (approval cohort)
intervention_dose: tazemetostat 800 mg PO BID, continuous 28-day cycles
indication: advanced epithelioid sarcoma with INI1/SMARCB1 loss
population_detail: 62 patients, ECOG 0-2, documented INI1 loss by IHC or biallelic SMARCB1 alteration; 1L and later lines
design: open-label phase 2 basket, epithelioid sarcoma cohort (NCT02601950)
median_dor_or_pfs: mDoR not reached (95% CI 9.2-NE); mPFS 5.5 mo
safety_summary: Unusually gentle for an active oral agent: G3+ treatment-related anemia 6% and weight loss 3%; two treatment-related serious AEs (seizure, haemoptysis); no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Pivotal cohort behind the FDA accelerated approval, which is confined to epithelioid sarcoma. For her this is mechanism precedent only: a different histology, and her SMARCB1 call is plasma-only against a strong prior that uterine smooth-muscle tumours retain INI1 (see excluded Kihara row). Any use in uLMS would be off-label extrapolation gated on tissue INI1 loss.

intervention_label: Tazemetostat across SWI/SNF-altered solid tumours (basket, INI1-negative cohort)
intervention_dose: tazemetostat 800 mg PO BID
indication: solid tumours with SWI/SNF alterations: rhabdoid tumours, synovial sarcoma, INI1-negative tumours of any histology, renal medullary carcinoma, poorly differentiated chordoma
population_detail: 129 patients across five cohorts; Cohort 3 (INI1-negative any histology, n=32) is the cohort a tissue-confirmed INI1-lost uLMS would have entered
safety_summary: G3+ treatment-related AEs in 10% across 129 patients; consistent with the benign profile seen in epithelioid sarcoma.
notes: The closest thing to data for an INI1-lost uLMS: a 9% response rate in INI1-negative non-epithelioid histologies, with the authors concluding single-agent EZH2 inhibition needs combination partners. No uLMS-specific EZH2 efficacy data exist anywhere, accrual is closed, and both BRD9 degraders in the SWI/SNF space have been discontinued (see excluded rows). This branch stays hypothetical until tissue INI1 IHC returns lost.

intervention_label: Afamitresgene autoleucel (SPEARHEAD-1)
intervention_dose: single IV infusion, transduced dose 1.0-10.0 x 10^9 T cells, after fludarabine/cyclophosphamide lymphodepletion
indication: advanced synovial sarcoma or myxoid round cell liposarcoma, HLA-A*02, MAGE-A4-expressing, after anthracycline- or ifosfamide-containing therapy
population_detail: 52 patients (44 synovial sarcoma, 8 MRCLS); median 3 prior lines; MAGE-A4 expression and HLA-A*02 required at screening
outcome: overall response rate by masked independent review
safety_summary: CRS in 71% (one G3); G3+ cytopenias near-universal (lymphopenia 96%, neutropenia 85%); no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Basis of the FDA approval (Tecelra), which reaches synovial sarcoma only. She clears the HLA-A*02 gate but sits outside the histology, and her MAGE-A4 status is untested; uLMS access would be trial-based (e.g. surgery-free cohorts or basket TCR-T programs), contingent on antigen IHC.

intervention_label: NY-ESO-1c259 TCR T cells (letetresgene autoleucel lineage) in synovial sarcoma
intervention_dose: single infusion of NY-ESO-1c259 TCR T cells after fludarabine 30 mg/m2 x4 + cyclophosphamide 1800 mg/m2 x2 lymphodepletion
indication: metastatic synovial sarcoma, HLA-A*02, NY-ESO-1-expressing
population_detail: 12 patients in the reported high-antigen, full-lymphodepletion cohort

outcomes.name: ORR
outcomes.notes: 6 of 12 confirmed responses; tumour shrinkage evolved over months

safety_summary: G3+ AEs in all 12 patients, dominated by lymphodepletion cytopenias; CRS in 5 of 12 (two G3); no fatal AEs.
notes: The clinical foundation for lete-cel, which uses this same NY-ESO-1c259 TCR. The registrational IGNYTE-ESO synovial sarcoma/MRCLS results had no PubMed-indexed primary publication as of August 2026, so this pilot is the citable evidence. No uLMS data exist for NY-ESO-1 TCR-T; her NY-ESO-1 expression is untested. CRS and cytopenia rates from the PMC full text.

intervention_label: IMA203 PRAME-directed TCR T cells (phase 1)
intervention_dose: single infusion, 3+3 dose escalation with dose extension, after lymphodepletion
indication: PRAME-positive recurrent/refractory solid tumours in HLA-A*02-positive patients (melanoma-dominant; sarcoma included)
population_detail: 41 patients started lymphodepletion, 40 treated; PRAME expression and HLA-A*02 required; confirmed responses enriched at higher dose and higher PRAME expression
design: first-in-human phase 1 dose escalation/extension (NCT03686124), interim report
safety_summary: MTD not reached; severe CRS 4.9% (2 of 41), no severe neurotoxicity; expected lymphodepletion cytopenias.
notes: The published PRAME TCR-T dataset her HLA type points at; melanoma-dominant with sarcoma patients included but no uLMS-specific efficacy reported. PRAME is frequently expressed in sarcomas including LMS, yet her own PRAME expression is untested; the trial screen carries the active IMA203 registration-track study. Brenetafusp, the PRAME ImmTAC, had no peer-reviewed clinical publication as of August 2026.

intervention_label: Tebentafusp (ImmTAC class precedent, IMCgp100-202)
intervention_dose: tebentafusp weekly IV with intra-patient step-up dosing
indication: previously untreated metastatic uveal melanoma, HLA-A*02:01-positive
population_detail: 378 HLA-A*02:01 patients randomised 2:1 vs investigator's choice (pembrolizumab, ipilimumab, or dacarbazine)
safety_summary: Cytokine-mediated and skin AEs dominate (rash 83%, pyrexia 76%, pruritus 69%), fading after the first 3-4 doses; discontinuation 2%; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Included as the proof that an off-the-shelf HLA-A*02:01-restricted bispecific TCR can move overall survival in a solid tumour. Everything else about it is uveal-melanoma-specific (gp100 target); its role in her dossier is to anchor the ImmTAC class, not to suggest tebentafusp itself.

intervention_label: Pembrolizumab monotherapy in STS (SARC028) - LMS cohort negative
intervention_dose: pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w
indication: advanced soft-tissue and bone sarcoma, up to 3 prior lines
population_detail: STS cohort n=40 evaluable, 10 per histology including 10 LMS
outcome: objective response, STS cohort (primary endpoint not met)
safety_summary: Typical PD-1 profile; G3+ anemia, lymphopenia and aPTT prolongation at 7% each in the STS cohort; immune-related SAEs included pneumonitis, adrenal insufficiency, nephritis.

toxicities.notes: among treatment-emergent serious AEs, both cohorts

notes: Half of the case against single-agent PD-1 in her histology: zero of ten LMS responses, while UPS and dedifferentiated liposarcoma carried the signal.

intervention_label: Nivolumab monotherapy in uterine LMS (negative phase 2)
intervention_dose: nivolumab 3 mg/kg IV q2w
indication: advanced uterine leiomyosarcoma, previously treated
population_detail: 12 patients, single centre; stage 1 of a 2-stage design; PD-L1 expression 20% of archival samples
design: single-arm phase 2, stopped at stage 1 for futility
safety_summary: G3+ events in 9 of 12 patients but only 3 attributed to nivolumab (abdominal pain, amylase/lipase rise, fatigue); the rest tracked disease progression.
notes: The other half of the case: the only uLMS-specific single-agent PD-1 trial, stopped for futility at 12 patients with no responses and 1.8-month PFS. Any checkpoint strategy for her needs a combination rationale. AE detail from the PMC full text.

intervention_label: Nivolumab +/- ipilimumab (Alliance A091401)
intervention_dose: nivolumab 3 mg/kg q2w; or nivolumab 3 mg/kg + ipilimumab 1 mg/kg q3w x4 then nivolumab q2w
indication: metastatic sarcoma after >=1 prior systemic line
population_detail: 85 treated across two non-comparative arms; LMS among enrolled histologies; responses in the combination arm included LMS and uterine sarcoma
safety_summary: Combination arm: G3+ anaemia 19%, hypotension 10%; treatment-related SAEs 26% vs 19% with monotherapy; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Establishes that dual checkpoint blockade retrieves a modest response rate in sarcoma where PD-1 alone fails; the authors sent the combination, not the monotherapy, forward. Supports combination or bispecific IO logic in her disease more than any single-agent plan.

intervention_label: Doxorubicin + pembrolizumab, first-line chemo-IO (phase 1/2)
intervention_dose: doxorubicin 45 or 75 mg/m2 + pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w
indication: advanced anthracycline-naive sarcoma (LMS the most common subtype, 11 of 37)
population_detail: 37 patients, single academic sarcoma centre; osteosarcoma, Ewing and alveolar/embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma excluded
outcome: objective response rate (primary endpoint not met)
safety_summary: No dose-limiting toxicities or unexpected safety signals; tolerability of the chemo-IO combination was the main positive finding.
notes: Shows anthracycline plus PD-1 is deliverable first line in sarcoma with PFS/OS that compare well with historical doxorubicin, though the response endpoint failed and durable responses clustered in UPS/DDLPS rather than LMS. Context for weighing chemo-first vs the ivonescimab seat. AE fallback: abstract and PMC text report no per-term G3 table beyond absence of DLTs.

intervention_label: Pembrolizumab in TMB-high solid tumours (KEYNOTE-158 prospective TMB analysis)
intervention_dose: pembrolizumab 200 mg IV q3w, up to 35 cycles
indication: previously treated advanced solid tumours across ten cohorts (no sarcoma cohort)
population_detail: 790 efficacy-evaluable, 102 tTMB-high (>=10 mut/Mb by FoundationOne CDx)
design: prospective biomarker analysis of a multicohort single-arm phase 2 (NCT02628067)

outcomes.name: TRAE_rate
outcomes.notes: grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs, tTMB-high safety population

safety_summary: G3-5 treatment-related AEs 15% in the tTMB-high group; one treatment-related fatal pneumonia; colitis the only recurring G3+ term.
notes: Underpins the tumour-agnostic TMB>=10 pembrolizumab approval. Her TMB is unmeasured and uLMS is rarely TMB-high, so this row exists to justify closing the TMB gap on tissue NGS, not to predict benefit. Sarcoma was not among the ten cohorts.

intervention_label: Ivonescimab vs pembrolizumab (HARMONi-2, NSCLC)
intervention_dose: ivonescimab 20 mg/kg IV q3w; comparator pembrolizumab 200 mg q3w
indication: PD-L1-positive advanced NSCLC, first line
population_detail: 398 patients in China; PD-L1 TPS >=1%; EGFR/ALK excluded
design: randomised double-blind phase 3 (HARMONi-2, NCT05499390), interim analysis
safety_summary: G3+ treatment-related AEs 29% vs 16% for pembrolizumab, the increment mostly VEGF-class effects; G3+ immune-related AEs similar (7% vs 8%).
notes: Why the PD-1xVEGF bispecific is credible: it beat pembrolizumab head-to-head on PFS in NSCLC. Zero published sarcoma efficacy data; the single-arm MSK trial (NCT07516925) is her only route, and the GOG-0250 row is the cautionary precedent that VEGF blockade added to chemo did nothing in uLMS. China-only trial; OS immature at this analysis.

intervention_label: Anlotinib in refractory STS (phase 2, LMS subset)
intervention_dose: anlotinib 12 mg PO daily d1-14 q21d
indication: refractory metastatic soft-tissue sarcoma after anthracycline, angiogenesis-inhibitor-naive
population_detail: 166 patients in China; LMS subset n=26, not uterine-specific
median_dor_or_pfs: mPFS 5.6 mo overall; 11 mo in the LMS subset
safety_summary: Cleanest of the VEGFR-TKIs in this space: G3+ hypertension 4.8%, triglyceride elevation 3.6%, pneumothorax 2.4%; no treatment-related deaths.
notes: Backs the anlotinib phase 3 in the trial screen: the 26-patient LMS subset did unusually well (11-month mPFS). Chinese population, subgroup not prespecified for inference, and no uterine breakdown; pneumothorax risk deserves attention given her lung disease.

intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy (International Registry of Lung Metastases)
intervention_dose: surgical resection of lung metastases; complete resection in 88%
indication: lung metastases from any primary; sarcoma 2173 of 5206 cases
population_detail: 5206 metastasectomies from 18 thoracic units; prognostic model built on resectability, disease-free interval, and number of lesions
safety_summary: Operative morbidity and mortality not reported in the abstract; the registry's message is selection: completeness of resection, DFI and lesion count drive outcome.
notes: The selection criteria that still govern metastasectomy decisions. Her roughly 23-month interval from primary resection to metastatic diagnosis sits in the favourable DFI band, but bilateral multifocal infiltrative disease argues against completeness of resection today; this becomes live only after systemic control.

intervention_label: Repeated pulmonary metastasectomy for leiomyosarcoma
intervention_dose: wedge or anatomic resection; repeat metastasectomy in 48% of LMS patients
indication: pulmonary metastases from sarcoma; LMS subset n=31 of 82
population_detail: single-institution series over 15 years; LMS patients presented with fewer metastases (mean 1.9) and were mostly female
outcome: median OS after metastasectomy, LMS vs other sarcoma
safety_summary: Surgical morbidity not summarised in the abstract; disease-free intervals before and after first metastasectomy were the independent survival predictors.
notes: LMS lung metastases behave more indolently than other sarcomas after resection, and repeat operations extend survival in selected patients. Selection bias is heavy: these were operable, often oligometastatic patients, which she currently is not.

intervention_label: Pulmonary metastasectomy for uterine malignancies (Japanese multicentre registry)
intervention_dose: pulmonary metastasectomy
indication: lung metastases from uterine primaries; sarcoma subset n=46 of 319
population_detail: Metastatic Lung Tumor Study Group of Japan, 1984-2016; risk-adjusted analysis by primary histology
outcome: 5-year OS after metastasectomy, uterine sarcoma subset

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: shorter DFI carried elevated adjusted hazard of death

safety_summary: Operative complications not reported in the abstract.
notes: The uterine-specific metastasectomy dataset: half of resected uterine-sarcoma patients alive at 5 years, with DFI over 12 months the main selector. Her DFI qualifies; her current bilateral distribution does not, pending systemic response.

intervention_label: SBRT for sarcoma pulmonary metastases (MSK series)
intervention_dose: stereotactic body radiotherapy to 95 pulmonary metastases
indication: sarcoma pulmonary metastases, including patients unfit for or declining resection
population_detail: 66 consecutive patients, median follow-up 36 months; oligometastatic and intrathoracic-only disease predicted longer survival
safety_summary: No G3+ toxicity; three G2 pneumonitis and one G2 esophagitis.
notes: Local control above 90% with essentially no high-grade toxicity makes SBRT the non-surgical consolidation option if induction converts her to oligoprogressive or oligoresidual disease. Baseline pulmonary reserve at 8,500 ft residence should enter any pneumonitis-risk discussion.

intervention_label: SBRT for sarcoma pulmonary metastases (Cleveland Clinic series)
intervention_dose: SBRT 30-34 Gy/1 fx, 48-50 Gy/4-5 fx, or 60 Gy/5 fx
indication: sarcoma lung metastases
population_detail: 50 patients, 109 lung metastases, 2005-2021; lesion size >4 cm predicted worse local control and survival

outcomes.name: other
outcomes.notes: 76% needed no new or changed systemic therapy after SBRT

safety_summary: Toxicity 16% overall across regimens, none clearly dose-dependent; terms include pneumonitis/fibrosis, chest-wall toxicity, dermatitis.

toxicities.notes: pneumonitis/fibrosis, chest wall, dermatitis; per-grade split not in abstract

notes: Adds the chemotherapy-deferral angle: most patients needed no systemic change for a year after lung SBRT. In her sequencing the same idea would apply only after induction, to consolidate residual disease.

exclusion_reason: Liposarcoma subgroup analysis; outside her histology. Read to check whether the phase 3 OS benefit generalises to LMS: it was concentrated in liposarcoma (OS HR 0.51), so the trial-level advantage should not be projected onto her. Caveat carried on the eribulin trial row.
intervention_label: Eribulin vs dacarbazine, liposarcoma subgroup

exclusion_reason: Program discontinued by the sponsor. Phase 1 in synovial sarcoma and SMARCB1-deficient tumours: ORR 2% (1 of 55), QTc prolongation dose-limiting. Read because a BRD9 degrader was the other clinical route at the SMARCB1 hypothesis; no development path remains.
intervention_label: FHD-609 (BRD9 degrader), phase 1

exclusion_reason: Program discontinued; monotherapy advancement halted for cardiac toxicity with modest late-line efficacy per the sponsor's own report. Primarily a medicinal-chemistry paper with phase 1 topline; with FHD-609 also stopped, both clinical BRD9 degraders in the SWI/SNF space are gone.
intervention_label: CFT8634 (BRD9 degrader), discovery report with phase 1 topline

exclusion_reason: Preclinical porcine feasibility study, outside clinical-evidence scope. Read because the Toronto in vivo lung perfusion trial (NCT02811523) in the trial screen rests on it; no human efficacy publication exists as of August 2026. The trial's doxorubicin >450 mg cumulative-dose exclusion is the sequencing conflict with LMS-04 induction.
intervention_label: In vivo lung perfusion with doxorubicin (preclinical)

exclusion_reason: Not an intervention study; IHC prevalence series. Read to weigh the SMARCB1 branch: 170 of 170 uterine smooth-muscle tumours retained SMARCB1 expression, and all 206 uterine mesenchymal tumours retained SMARCB1. This is the hard prior against her plasma-only SMARCB1 frameshift being a tumour feature, and it is why tissue INI1 IHC gates the entire EZH2 branch.
intervention_label: SMARCB1/SMARCA4/SMARCA2 IHC in uterine mesenchymal tumours (context for EZH2 branch)

exclusion_reason: Wrong setting: adjuvant therapy for resected localized STS, not metastatic disease. Read while checking the anlotinib evidence base for the phase 3 in the trial screen.
intervention_label: Anlotinib adjuvant vs placebo in localized high-grade STS

exclusion_reason: Superseded for this dossier by two larger, more recent sarcoma-lung-SBRT series in the same population (Lebow 2023, Asha 2023) that carry the included rows; findings concordant (95% lesion control).
intervention_label: SBRT for sarcoma lung metastases (Florida series)
